content.comment_body: Hello all, After years of successfully using [product_name] version [version_no] on Mac OS Mojave, I upgraded to Catalina. I downloaded the 1.39GB upgrade file from the [company_name] site. After extracting everything, running the setup icon in the NoVM folder does nothing; no installation starts. Am I missing anything in the upgrade process? Any help is appreciated.

Start the install.htm file and follow the instructions. For Mac OS X: Double-click Setup after download. Make sure Java is installed (get it from Apple's website if needed). The compressed installer should be automatically expanded by StuffIt Expander; if not, expand manually with StuffIt Expander 6.0 or newer. If installation issues persist after expanding, confirm you used StuffIt Expander. For ongoing problems, contact technical support. Note: [product_name] does not support all Mac versions. The supported operating systems for [product_name] [version_no] are Windows XP, 7, 8, 10 (with hardware requirements 500 MB free space, 512 MB RAM, etc.), Mac OS X 10.7 through 10.11, and tested Linux distributions. Recommended Java Runtime Environment is 1.8.0_121. In your situation, consider submitting a support request.

The issue is that Mac OS Catalina (10.15.x) no longer runs any 32-bit software. Mac OS 10.14 previously warned users if a program needed updating but still allowed running 32-bit code. For a limited time, it's possible to stay on 10.14 with ongoing security updates, but it's not ideal in the long term. If you have a Mac with Catalina preinstalled, a workaround is to use a virtual machine (for example, Linux Mint with VirtualBox) and run the [product_name] Linux version until [company_name] releases a Mac version compatible with 64-bit systems. This is similar to legacy code problems on Windows 10. Due to the small user base, updates seem to be delayed.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face compatibility problems with [product_name] following a MacOS update from Mojave to Catalina, primarily because Catalina does not support 32-bit apps and the [company_name] software is not yet available in a 64-bit version for newer MacOS. Users are frustrated by the absence of timely software updates and clear compatibility information from [company_name].
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [company_name] software to be compatible with the latest MacOS versions and for installation and upgrades to be straightforward, with clear guidance on system compatibility and update availability.
